commentary: Kicking off planning for our employee wellness program launching January 2027 at Bellmark Industries. Excited to build something our 400 team members will actually use.
Great few days at the regional HR conference in Memphis. Reconnected with peers across Tennessee and came home with a notebook full of ideas for our benefits strategy.
Open enrollment season is around the corner. My advice to fellow HR leaders: start your communications early and repeat the important dates often. Clarity beats cleverness.
DEI work is a marathon, not a sprint. Grateful for the volunteers on our committee at Bellmark who keep showing up and doing the quiet, consistent work.
Leadership lesson I keep relearning: close the loop the first time. A quick follow-up email today saves three confused ones tomorrow.
Renewing my SHRM certification this cycle. Twenty years in HR and I still learn something new in every recert module. The day you stop learning is the day to hand over the keys.
Culture is what you tolerate and what you celebrate. As HR leaders we set that thermostat every single day, whether we mean to or not.
Manager one-on-ones are the highest-leverage hour in my week. No agenda too small, no concern too early. Half of retention happens in those conversations.
Onboarding done right sets the tone for everything that follows. A new hire's first week should feel welcoming, not like a stack of forms and a login problem.
Wrapped up our fall benefits fair at Bellmark today. Nothing beats sitting down face to face with employees and walking through their choices for next year.
A Saturday morning walk at Percy Warner Park clears my head better than any productivity app. HR is a people job, and you can't pour from an empty cup.
Proud of our team as we move into open enrollment. Months of prep, vendor calls, and DocuSign setup come down to making the process feel simple for every employee.
Grateful this Thanksgiving season for a team that cares, a company that invests in its people, and a community here in Nashville that feels like home.
Spent the evening at Calvary Hill Church choir rehearsal. Singing with that group is my reminder that the best teams listen to each other as much as they perform.
As the year closes, I am reviewing our workforce plans for 2026. Thoughtful headcount planning is one of the most respectful things an HR team can do for employees.
New year, same core belief: people do their best work when they feel seen. Setting that intention for our HR team at Bellmark heading into 2026.
Started a beginner yoga habit this month. Turns out the same patience I preach to new managers applies to holding a balance pose. Progress over perfection.
Deep in the design phase for our January 2027 wellness program. Meeting with vendors this week to shape screenings, mental health support, and incentives that actually move the needle.
Reading John Grisham on the weekend and leadership books during the week. Good storytelling and good management have more in common than people think: both are about understanding motive.
Hosted a manager development workshop today on giving feedback that lands. The best managers I know deliver hard messages with genuine care. That combination is a skill you can build.
Attended a Middle Tennessee SHRM chapter event tonight. Nothing recharges me like a room full of HR people swapping war stories and real solutions. Proud of our local community.
Reminder to fellow people leaders: benefits are a promise, not a perk. When someone is going through a hard season, how we handle their claim is what they will remember about us.
Southern Sunday dinners with family are my favorite reset button. Good food, no phones, and the kind of conversation that reminds you why the work matters in the first place.
Twenty years into HR and I still believe the fundamentals win: listen first, communicate clearly, follow through. Everything else is a tool in service of those three.
